name: Zell am Ziller
kurzbeschreibung: Musical heart of the Zillertal, featuring the Gauderfest and the Zillertaler Arena.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The market town of Zell am Ziller is located at 575 metres above sea level in the heart of the Zillertal valley within the Tyrolean district of Schwaz, precisely at the confluence of the Ziller and Gerlosbach rivers. Home to around 1,750 residents, this historic market forms the geographic, administrative, and educational heart of the valley. Enclosed by the Tux Alps to the west and the Kitzbühel Alps to the east, the town brings together vibrant folk culture, century-old brewing heritage, and premier leisure facilities. As a historic deanery seat and primary gateway to the Zillertal Arena—the valley's largest ski domain—Zell am Ziller plays an outstanding role in Tyrolean tourism.

Geschichte

Around 700–800 AD, monks from the Archbishopric of Salzburg founded a monastic outpost ("Celle") along the Gerlosbach to convert local communities. The parish was documented in 1187, and the town name appeared as Celles in 1188. For centuries, the river Ziller formed an imperial boundary: the eastern bank with Zell belonged to Salzburg, while the western bank belonged to Tyrol and the Diocese of Brixen. Zell became a district court seat in 1592. The town is inextricably linked to Zillertal Bier, Tyrol's oldest private brewery founded in 1500, and the historic Gauder Fest, dating back to 1428. Recognised as UNESCO intangible cultural heritage, this oldest spring folk festival in Austria features the potent Gauderbock bock beer, traditional Ranggeln wrestling, and colourful parades. The Deanery Church of St. Vitus was rebuilt between 1772 and 1778 as an octagonal domed hall with magnificent frescoes by court painter Franz Anton Zeiller.

Anreise

Zell am Ziller is easily accessible in the middle Zillertal valley. Drivers exit the Inntal motorway A12 at Wiesing/Zillertal and follow the federal highway B169 for approximately 20 kilometres directly to Zell am Ziller. From the east, the scenic Gerlos Alpine Road B165 connects from Salzburg's Pinzgau over the Gerlos Pass into town. By rail, passengers travel to Jenbach station and transfer to the Zillertalbahn narrow-gauge railway, which operates every half hour to Zell am Ziller station. From the station square, regional VVT buses provide frequent connections into the Gerlos Valley and towards Mayrhofen.

Tipps

In winter, the Zillertal Arena offers 150 kilometres of slopes and 52 lifts reaching altitudes above 2,500 metres, boasting Austria's longest continuous valley descent with 1,930 metres of vertical drop. At the valley station of the Rosenalmbahn, the Arena Coaster alpine rollercoaster provides year-round thrills with banked turns and 540-degree loops. The 5,000-square-metre BrauKunstHaus at Zillertal Bier takes visitors through an interactive exhibition exploring centuries of brewing followed by beer tastings. In the southern district, the Zillertal Regional Museum at the historic Ental homestead from 1713 showcases rural heritage and traditional farming tools.
